Seminar Title:

Hesperetin and ZnO-NP loaded CMC-GG bio-polymeric nanocomposite for anticancer, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory properties and its biocompatibility studies in Drosophila melanogaster

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Student

Venue:

Contact:

Abstract:

Carboxymethyl Cellulose-Guargum based polymeric nanocomposite incorporated with biogenic synthesized ZnO-NP and hesperetin (CMC-GG/ZnO/Hsp) was synthesized to develop a phytochemical-based nanomaterial by following a simple synthetic procedure. In this study, hesperetin, a natural citrus flavonoid and green synthesized ZnO-NP was by entrapped within Carboxymethyl Cellulose-Guargum derived nanocomposite. CMC-GG/ZnO/Hsp were characterized using XRD, FTIR, SEM. High loading percentage of hesperetin in polymeric nanocomposites revealed excellent incorporation efficiency. In addition, pH responsive release behavior of hesperetin from nanocomposites exhibited sustained and faster release. IC 50 value of CMC-GG/ZnO/Hsp were used against SW-480 cell line. Synergistic effect d of ZnO and hesperetin was observed in all the experiments. Experimental outcome confirmed excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) mediated cytotoxicity and higher degree of nuclear damage followed by increased mortality of SW-4800 cell cell after treatment with hesperetin and ZnO-loaded nanocomposite. Moreover, this composite resulted in enhanced antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. For invivo studies, Drosophila melanogaster was used to check the biocompatibility of this CMC GG/ZnO/Hsp nanocomposite. Cytoxicity and genotoxicity studies in the tissue confirmed that it is safer for oral consumption for the flies. Further, the behavioral studies conducted had no significant effect on the flies.
